headline: THE EXECUTION-QUALITY HYPOTHESIS IS REFUTED. L5 residual loses -0.1867/unit; ours loses -0.1855/unit. Indistinguishable. The difference is the MATCHED:RESIDUAL RATIO, not fill quality.

item8_decomposition.the_correct_comparison: L5 residual P&L per unit, computed on EXACTLY our measure (cost of the excess side at its average own price, versus what that side redeemed at settlement)
item8_decomposition.verdict: statistically indistinguishable. L5 is adversely selected on residual to the SAME degree we are.
item8_decomposition.my_prior_framing_was_WRONG: last turn I reported his residual as fairly priced (alpha +0.0043, z 0.8) against our -0.3994/unit in the 0.35-0.50 band. That compared his alpha on ALL FILLS against our realized loss on STRANDED LEGS -- two different conditioning sets, which is the exact category error I had warned about one turn earlier. Corrected here, the two measures agree.
item8_decomposition.band_reading: in the band where our residual actually sits, L5 loses -0.3027/unit and we lose -0.3994/unit -- the same order of magnitude, not a gap that execution quality could explain. Our outlier bands (0.00-0.20 at n=5 legs, 0.65+ at n=3) are the underpowered ones.

order_placement.reading: L5 is overwhelmingly a maker, and his maker alpha is MONOTONE in price: adverse at cheap prices, favourable at dear ones. He is not uniformly well-executed; he is favourite-biased, which is the same effect already in the record.

item8_decomposition.queue_position: NOT MEASURABLE on either side. Our pre-submit rows carry our_position_within_level UNKNOWN; L5 public data carries no order-level events at all, only fills. No queue claim can be made for or against.
item8_decomposition.market_movement_and_depth: not isolable as an explanation, because the outcome gap the decomposition was meant to explain does not exist once the conditioning sets are matched.
item8_decomposition.venue_differences: L5 is Polymarket International, we are PMUS. The venues differ in fee schedule and in incentive programs, and THAT is where his advantage actually sits: his reconstructed trading P&L is -$2,829 against roughly $71,500 of credited incentives. He did not out-execute us on residual; he was paid to carry it.

what_the_difference_actually_IS.reading: residual costs both of us about 0.186 a unit. L5 earns matched profit on 5.30 contracts for every residual unit; we earn it on 1.786, against a breakeven of about 2.012. He clears it on COMPLETION RATE, not on fill quality.

item7_sensitivity.question: does arm B (aggressive repricing) survive queue and latency degradation?
item7_sensitivity.reading: B beats A on the holdout at every fill probability tested, down to 0.25. The advantage is robust to queue uncertainty in this sample. Note the train column turns POSITIVE at p_fill 0.25 while pairs fall to 5.6 -- part of that apparent gain is simply fewer completions, the refusal pattern again.
item7_sensitivity.latency_knob_was_INERT_and_here_is_why: lag of 0, 1 and 2 ticks gave byte-identical results. Diagnosed rather than reported as a finding: all 7 complement fills in the tape occur 6, 2, 2, 2, 4, 6 and 2 ticks after the last reprice, so a 1-2 tick lag cannot block any of them. At ~4.4s median cadence a 1-tick lag already models 4.4s of latency, four times the measured 1.02s cancel round-trip. Real repricing latency is SUB-TICK on this tape and therefore unobservable -- not harmless.

deliverable.smallest_safe_change: NONE to the money path this turn. The lever the evidence points at -- raising completions per residual unit -- is served by completion_requote(), which already exists, is already stricter than the fader on the cancel race, and is DISABLED by an unset L5_COMPLETION_REQUOTE. The telemetry row making that state visible shipped in d29a4bf7.
deliverable.why_not_the_099_cap: measured again and unchanged: train -0.63 -> +0.45, HOLDOUT -2.53 -> -2.83. It buys 3 completions between 0.96 and 0.99 whose dearer pairs do not pay for themselves out of sample. One of four real fills converts (2300z, +/bin/bash.3864), which is a single observation.
minimum_additional_real_time_measurement: our queue position within the level at submit and on every book change -- currently UNKNOWN in our own pre-submit rows
per-level depth at and around our own quote price, not only the touch, at <=1s cadence
order-level events retained beyond the container: submit, ack, partial fill, cancel request, cancel ack, terminal state, each venue-timestamped
one bounded campaign with L5_COMPLETION_REQUOTE=YES and nothing else changed, which is the only way to observe real cancel/replace outcomes at sub-tick latency
